ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Win rate is not the whole story.
Not even close.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors track wins and losses and call it a day. 55% sounds great. But if your wins pay -115 and your losses cost -115, you are still bleeding money on bad lines.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Units fix that. One unit is a fixed stake, usually 1% to 2% of your bankroll. Every pick is sized. Every result is tracked in dollars, not just ticks on a scoreboard.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example: two bettors, both 55-45 over 100 bets.
Bettor A: flat units, good lines. Net +8u.
Bettor B: chased losses, bad lines. Net -4u.
Same win rate. Opposite outcomes.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
54.3% win rate. +46.6 units. 9.3% ROI.
That is what the full picture looks like. Win rate gets you in the door. Units tell you if it is working.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate is a headline. Units are the truth. Save this if you want to actually track your bets the right way.
